Define hyperplanes for ultraviolet arrangements

Source: R/make_ultraviolet_ineqmat.R
make_ultraviolet_ineqmat.Rd

Named to draw a parallel with the the "infrared" arrangements (see make_infrared_ineqmat()), the "ultraviolet" arrangements are also primarily intended to study voice leadings in conjunction with vl_signvector(). They evaluate whether a voice leading involves contrary motion in equal but opposite amounts, such as when the soprano rises two semitones while the bass falls 2 semitones. In this, the ultraviolet arrangements are complementary to the white arrangements of make_white_ineqmat(). Unlike many hyperplane arrangements in musicMCT, the ultraviolet arrangements do not reflect transpositional equivalence.

Usage

make_ultraviolet_ineqmat(card)

Arguments

card

The cardinality of the scale(s) to be studied

Value

A matrix with card+1 columns and k rows, where k is the nth triangular number

Details

Combinatorial features of these arrangements are described in Richard Stanley, "A Zonotope Associated with Graphical Degree Sequences," in Applied Geometry and Discrete Mathematics: The Victor Klee Festschrift, 555-570, edited by Peter Gritzmann and Bernd Sturmfels (American Mathematical Society, 1990).

See also

make_infrared_ineqmat() and make_white_ineqmat() for related hyperplane arrangements.

Examples

uv_trichord_ineqmat <- make_ultraviolet_ineqmat(3)
voice_leading_1 <- c(-1, 1, 0)
vl_signvector(voice_leading_1, ineqmat=uv_trichord_ineqmat)
#> [1]  0 -1  1

# The first entry of the sign vector is 0 because the bass and alto voices
# move in a perfectly counterbalanced wedge. The second entry of the sign vector
# compares bass and soprano; the third entry compares alto and soprano:
print(uv_trichord_ineqmat)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]       [,4]
#> [1,]    1    1    0 -0.3333333
#> [2,]    1    0    1 -0.6666667
#> [3,]    0    1    1 -1.0000000

# If this voice leading is transposed ("Tinctoris transformed") up a semitone,
# then it will lie on no ultraviolet hyperplanes.
voice_leading_2 <- voice_leading_1 + 1
vl_signvector(voice_leading_2, ineqmat=uv_trichord_ineqmat)
#> [1] 1 1 1
